title: Mapping a mangrove walkway
paragraphs: A youth nature group wanted to improve signs along a mangrove walkway. Instead of replacing every sign immediately, the members first observed where visitors stopped, turned back or asked for directions. They recorded these moments on a shared map for six weekends.

The map revealed an unexpected pattern. Visitors rarely became confused at the longest paths; most difficulties occurred at two short junctions where several arrows were visible at once. The group installed temporary signs at those junctions and kept the old signs elsewhere.

During the next four weekends, fewer visitors requested directions. The result was encouraging, but the group remained cautious because the second observation period was shorter and the weather was calmer. Its report recommended keeping the temporary signs while collecting more evidence before making permanent changes.
